# Transport v4 vectors

Vectors in this directory are generated from the single
`stability/transport_v4_schema.json` registry by
`scripts/generate-transport-v4-vectors.mjs`.

Do not add hand-authored protocol bytes here. Input values and malformed-case
recipes belong to the registry. `corpus.json` contains generated bytes and
expected rejection codes; every case runs through the reference validator.
The manifest binds every generated file, schema revision/hash and byte digest.
Go, Rust, Swift and TypeScript constants are outputs of the same generator.

`rekey_credit.json` contains 48 full-Session response-count and retained-credit
arithmetic cases. It includes the initial epoch in the fixed epoch limit, uses
exact rational drift and the design's integer error allowance, preserves partial
balances and saturates before large idle multiplication. Four independent native
test consumers run through `make transport-v4-rekey-credit-check`. These pure
projections establish no live original base/causal ACK anchor, once-only INIT
deduction, pending-round exclusion, clock continuity or actual service/cleanup
reservation. The signed Artifact interval is the service responsibility; shorter
root/policy lifetimes cannot shrink it, and no implicit time skew is added.

`crypto_usage.json` contains 28 arithmetic cases for actual seal/open inputs
under both fixed profiles. Ciphertext includes the tag; authentication blocks
round AAD and payload separately and include the length block even for empty
inputs. Maximum integer cases test charge arithmetic, not permission to invoke
an AEAD on inputs exceeding real frame, library or usage limits. Fixed caps are
distinct from their still-required independent aggregate cryptographic proof;
live reservation, counter ownership, cancellation and root-age gates remain
unqualified. Independent Go, Rust, Swift and TypeScript consumers recompute all
charges using the generated registry and check block rounding and strict types.
Run `make transport-v4-crypto-usage-check`; this is charge arithmetic only and
does not qualify live cap enforcement or AEAD invocation.

`time_arithmetic.json` covers rational drift, outward rounding, complete RTT,
source and elapsed-measurement uncertainty, original anchor age/width, deadline
projection and lower-bound proving increments. Exact decimal strings are the
vector interface; they are not clock samples or authentication evidence.
Quantities and results are uint64 with checked uint128 intermediates. Quantization
bounds observed minus ideal monotonic increments before drift conversion; the
vectors include a high-drift counterexample to applying that error afterward.
Four independent native test consumers and the generator reference check all
37 vectors plus rounding and inverse inequalities over rational ranges. Run
`make transport-v4-time-check` for this common corpus. Real source/profile/
incarnation, suspend, owner, timer and runtime qualifications remain required.
A projected wakeup never proves validity or extends an original deadline.

`resources.json` contains synthetic byte/work/item composition cases. Complete
owner keys and immutable charge bindings determine deduplication within each
legal feature combination; maxima apply only after those sums. Non-SDK control
boundaries remain separate. These cases neither establish real provider charges
nor implement reservation, ownership transfer, reference exit or physical caps.
Four independent native test references consume these vectors through
`make transport-v4-resources-check`, with additional malformed-input, identity
and overflow checks.

`resource_costs.json` pins partial byte costs for codec body buffers, the
permanent bitmap and fixed application responsibilities at every supported
profile. Its coefficients are generated from the resource formula registry;
the common scope domain and signed K limits reuse their existing declarations.
These costs do not constitute a complete admission vector or frame-fit proof.
Actual objects, short-work protection, indexes, simultaneous copies and cleanup
tails still require their complete owner charges before admission.
All four independent resource consumers also check every partial-cost case.

The Go test-only canonical syntax reader consumes all positive `corpus.json`
fixtures and its syntax-negative subset. This includes the explicit `cbor_syntax`
cases for complete uint64s, shortest headers, malformed lengths, depth, key
order, UTF-8 and Unicode text. It reads syntax-affecting descriptors directly
from the generated registry; byte-string documents keep their original bytes.
The separate Go field layer checks membership, required fields, scalar types,
widths, constraints and nested/embedded shapes against generated declarations.
It consumes the field-negative subset, excluding map-rule oracles that reuse
field error names. Required/unknown-field mutations cover the 76 schemas with
root positives in this corpus; nested-only and separate-corpus maps do not
receive that exhaustive mutation set. Cross-field variants and semantic rules
remain unfinished. Its independent
Unicode 15.1 NFC reference uses checksummed repository tables, all 19,074
normalization cases and the normative Part1 scalar complement. These tests do
not qualify runtime allocation, four-language receiver behavior or IDNA/Origin.

`noise.json` preserves schema-owned fixed public inputs, captured Snow 0.10.0
messages, final handshake hash, canonical Split outputs and initial-root bytes
for both required profiles. The generator checks public encodings and root
derivation and expands every-byte, truncation and extension negatives; it does
not implement Noise. Rust and the Go reference execute both profiles. The Go
reference uses pinned flynn/noise source with a checked public-key-length
interface extension; unchanged upstream additionally compares X25519. The
opaque prologue is a library fixture; these tests
do not authenticate Flowersec admission or qualify READY/records/rekey, runtime
key ownership, independent cryptographic composition or real providers.

NamespaceCapacity, HeadSignerDelegation and FreshnessHead samples include
complete 514/683/795-byte maximal encodings, missing/unknown fields,
noncanonical bytes, required two-position floors and time-order negatives.
Four separate domains bind capacity, delegation, Head signature input and
complete signed Head digest. Signature bytes in structural samples remain
public fixtures. Stateless reference checks cover exact namespace/capacity/
delegation binding, original signer expiry, checked cohort arithmetic and
componentwise mature floors. They do not authenticate independent TrustConfig,
publication policy or signatures, install a State, advance durable continuity,
reserve subscription resources or qualify SDK/provider implementations.

RevokedCertificateEntry, RevokedLeaseEntry and IssuerAuthorizationImpact have
56/92/76-byte maximal encodings. Their vectors retain complete digest/cohort/
time evidence, and only the two declared issuer impact positions admit
canonical null. Schema-free CBOR and unrelated uint64 fields still reject it.
Reference checks match certificate/parent originals and compute componentwise
maxima for two original issuer permissions. Null requires independently proven
absence of that class permission; it never represents missing history. These
references do not prove full State membership, permission-history completeness,
namespace/generation/capacity attribution, H_c compliance, permanent frontier
installation, trust retirement, once retention or actual reference cleanup.

RevokedIssuerEntry preserves a nonempty, uniquely sorted list of original
IssuerAuthorizationImpact records for one issuer key. Its reference byte/count
bounds are projected from an independently authenticated NamespaceCapacity;
the count cannot exceed its State byte bound divided by the 44-byte minimum
complete impact encoding. Schema-declared capacity arrays can exceed the
ordinary 1035-item reference parser limit. Missing context, unrepresentable
bounds, oversized input and forged/truncated counts fail before input copying
or array-slot allocation as applicable. Other fields keep their original
grammar and caps. The union uses every supplied original; history completeness,
authenticated purposes and namespace attribution remain external. This is not
a complete State parser or proof of physical SDK subscription capacity.

PublicationPolicy and CredentialRevocationPolicy each have a 162-byte maximum
canonical encoding. Reference tests independently intersect staleness and signer
lifetime requirements, check the fixed publication envelope and complete Head/
delegation durations, and calculate deadlines from the original active Head,
delegation, trust and credential timestamps. Current time, remaining signer
life and policy labels cannot refresh deadlines or bypass incompatibility.
The authenticated original dependency closure and active pairing remain external.

`api_results.json` contains native Read/Write/Transfer/Close/cleanup fixtures, separate
from the CBOR wire corpus. JSON tags `$bigint` and `$bytes` preserve uint64 and
byte values for tooling; they are not a wire encoding. Explicit success/error
oracles cover end offsets, retained cursor frontiers, contextual empty results,
target failures, strict error tuples and independent direction/cleanup facts.
The same API schema generates internal Go, Rust, Swift and TypeScript types.
The error allocation currently covers only the registered L0 subset; the
cleanup detail is not the complete cross-object lifecycle API. Trusted method
and owner context, authentication, unique handoff and physical cleanup still
require runtime implementation and qualification.

`application_headers.json` contains maximal base and business-error headers and
explicit missing/forbidden-field, kind and malformed-encoding negatives.
Kinds and field sets derive from the same registry. Ordinary execution digest
inputs and SHA-256 outputs appear in `domains.json`; tests independently
assemble their byte inputs. Response matching requires the original request
and cannot replace its deadlines, admission mode or limits. SDK refusal, terminal
and Resume variants, real channel/serial owners and actual dispatch remain
separate unfinished work.

The four business-error variants carry a nonzero application code and preserve
execution/transient request identity. Their maximal headers are 127/57 bytes.
Unknown legal codes and known-definition size mismatches have distinct metadata
classifications; all business payloads retain the original response limit.
The error-schema digest hashes exact pre-registered opaque canonical bytes,
bounded by the local per-method metadata ceiling. It does not interpret schema
syntax or load codecs. Local catalog matching covers each entire ErrorDefinition;
actual codec delivery, aggregate metadata accounting and typed result ownership
remain unqualified.

`fragment_states.json` executes schema-owned live-association transition
sequences, including mixed directions, abort confirmation, STOP coalescing,
stale STOP, ordering and rejection without partial state changes. Its BEGIN
header is an opaque structural fixture; trusted application header/content
validation is an explicit external input to the reference. It does not qualify
an application header variant, authentication, Session-wide reservation,
provider I/O or physical cleanup. The model keeps only BEGIN high-water and
live request/response associations, with no serial history table.

Run `make transport-v4-vectors` to regenerate. Run
`make transport-v4-schema-check` or the generator's `--check` to compare all
files without writing them. Changed, missing or unregistered files fail the
check; it never repairs them silently.

Coverage is explicitly `draft_cbor_fields_only`. Samples include nested
certificate and activation structures, hello/admission, READY, rekey and
terminal/credit constraints. Their signature/proof/key bytes are deterministic
public test material, not trusted credentials. Encoded certificate and proof
fields retain their original canonical bytes and require their source context.

`errors.json` is the executable ERROR/CLOSE/GOAWAY/FSA4/OPEN_ACCEPT subset of
the CBOR corpus. Registry-driven cases cover each allocated rejection and
Session/Stream code, target fields, optional retry hints, rejection sentinels,
zero-data OPEN frontiers and normal close reasons. It includes malformed
encoding and field cases; removing or relabeling those cases fails verification.
Generated SDK registries retain the same definitions and qualification boundary.
These cases do not establish authenticated ownership, durable admission state,
retry authority, real termination or public API behavior.

`fragments.json` is the generated binary framing corpus for the reliable ordered
RPC stream. The registry fixes the four-byte big-endian length prefix, four
fragment kinds, serial/header rules, and the 16 KiB complete-fragment cap. It
covers exact BEGIN, DATA, ABORT and STOP_OUTPUT boundaries plus truncation,
unknown-kind, zero-serial, and non-exact-length failures. The corpus validates
framing and owned byte copies only; message ordering, request semantics,
authorization, and runtime channel ownership remain qualification work.

A PING payload is an isolated map, not a plaintext wire frame. OPEN samples
derive their digest from the unsigned map; negative mutations can deliberately
retain a forged digest. Live metadata registration, authentication and session
ownership still need qualification. Text uses pinned Unicode 15.1 NFC tables and rejects
noncanonical input instead of normalizing received bytes. The DNS reference uses
fixed IDNA data and the canonical DNS/IP host grammar. The Origin reference
checks canonical tuples under the registered scheme/default-port mappings;
custom schemes, actual Origin admission, route provider validation and four-SDK
text processing remain unqualified. The corpus does not establish handshake cryptography,
state-machine, cross-SDK, provider or production qualification.

`text.json` contains issuer DNS/host and strict wire A-label/IP cases, including
Unicode 15.1 mapping, IDNA2008/context rejection, numeric-alias rejection and
the unique hexadecimal IPv6 spelling. DNS primitives are separate from the
complete host grammar, which also excludes numeric final DNS labels.
The official nontransitional UTS46 corpus runs separately in the schema gate.

OriginPolicy samples reject alias ports, multiple values and non-visible bytes,
including trailing newlines after explicit ports. Origin sets sort by complete
canonical CBOR bytes, including the text-length head. The reference proves the
maximum encoding size for its current registered tuples; it does not qualify
browser header control or listener enforcement of the signed policy.

Route samples cover the signed network/local variants, physical tunnel roles,
mixed carrier legs, Candidate namespace identity and the exact complete-route
digest. Tests verify that the containing map supplies path kind even when caller
context differs, and reject incorrect carrier tuples or forbidden local TLS fields.
Real dependency closure and provider/SDK qualification remain separate gates.

Artifact samples cover all 28 required fields, complete policy variants, signed
time ordering, feature authorization and candidate priority/ID ordering. They
reject mixed local/network candidate lists, repeated IDs even under different
priorities, and missing fields. Full-width idle and issuance durations retain
uint64 values; the per-direction bootstrap credit and profile-specific RPC
fields have independent bounds. These structural checks do not implement idle
timers, negotiation, admission, once storage or application token recovery.

The complete Artifact boundary is exactly 65536 bytes. Increasing its otherwise
legal audience by one byte produces a 65537-byte negative that passes every
other field rule. This prevents individually legal candidates or their count
from bypassing the whole-object cap. Structural signatures remain test data.
Artifact digest/signature vectors preserve their full/unsigned projections;
the complete SessionContract digest uses a separate domain from ServiceContract.

PoolSelectionSet samples derive from the original complete signed Artifact and
an exact index list. Their derivation inputs are retained in the generated
corpus and revalidated with each run. They preserve all selected candidates,
including distinct candidates at one endpoint, and generate both independent
candidate-set/route-set digest inputs. The 1/2/16-member sizes are 94/150/934
bytes. Structural mutations reject bad encoding and false membership. Reference
tests also reject mismatched PoolSelectionRef, Artifact, proof, source context
and FSB4 winner pairs; no result grants trust, once or activation authority.

Grant samples bind the complete tunnel route, ordered endpoint references,
parent Session deadline, independent namespaces and unsigned digest/signature
inputs. Endpoint HELLO checks the complete signed certificate digest, tenant and
logical role against its embedded Grant. Maximal structural samples include
both WS legs with 16 pins and 8 Origins each and a complete P-256 certificate;
their pinned encoded lengths include all map, array and byte-string overhead.
Actual credential trust, expected audiences, issuer projection, possession,
ledger ownership and claim-time capacity remain separate verification duties.

TLS policy samples cover strict CA/pin variants, the registered DER certificate
profile, positive bounded windows and digest-sorted pin sets. Placeholder hashes
do not establish actual DER validity, TLS verification or browser behavior.
Maximum-encoding samples measure schema widths, not feasible certificate dates.

`signatures.json` contains actual Ed25519 signatures over the existing domain
inputs and the RFC8032 test 1 known answer, with 13 positives and 104 negatives.
Mutations cover message/key changes, signature corruption, exact lengths and
S+L scalar rejection. Run `make transport-v4-signature-check` to exercise the
same vectors with Go crypto/ed25519, Rust ring, Swift Crypto and TypeScript
noble. The deterministic fixture generator reproduces the RFC signature;
CryptoKit documents randomized signing, so fresh Swift output is verified
without requiring byte equality. Full strict A/R point, nonidentity and
prime-order subgroup predicates remain unqualified. Domain inputs preserve
structural objects with placeholder keys/signatures; signing those inputs with
the fixture key does not prove embedded signer identity, credential trust,
Noise/post-handshake correctness or runtime/provider interoperability.

`strict_signatures.json` binds the schema-owned Pure Ed25519 policy to the
primitive fixtures plus all eight A/R torsion classes, mixed-order points,
noncanonical encodings, scalar bounds, prehash and cross-domain substitutions.
Adversarial group fixtures satisfy the cofactored equation, so rejection cannot
be attributed only to a broken signature equation. Generation uses the pinned
Noble public point APIs with public scalars. Go, Rust, Swift and TypeScript
references consume these bytes with explicit A/R subgroup checks and signer
post-validation gates. Swift uses exact swift-sodium 0.11.0 and checks fresh
CryptoKit signatures with libsodium 1.0.22. Execution evidence currently covers
macOS arm64; independent adapter review, other deployments and runtime ownership
remain unqualified.
The generation commands require the existing locked TypeScript dependencies;
the Makefile targets ensure them before generating or checking artifacts.

`profile_dh.json` binds the DH policy to fixed public fixture material. The
corpus includes X25519 RFC7748 anchors, all 19 noncanonical residues with both
high-bit values and their canonical forms, nonzero twist inputs, low-order
zero results, local clamping and length boundaries. P-256 cases cover exact
SEC1 uncompressed encodings, invalid points/scalars, shared x-coordinate
agreement, and a valid point whose scalar-1 DH output is all zero. That same
point with scalar 2 must succeed, so it cannot be rejected by a point blacklist.

`make transport-v4-dh-check` runs the corpus through Go, Rust, Swift and
TypeScript reference adapters. The generated policy and profile constants are
shared; each adapter uses its selected public library. The generator and
TypeScript consumer share Noble. Tests compare all accepted outputs, stable
failure results and original input preservation where inputs are mutable.
These checks cover macOS arm64 execution, not runtime key ownership, entropy,
actual Noise/rekey inputs, authenticated original transcripts, KDF ordering,
provider deployment or independent cryptographic composition.

`domains.json` records exact signing/AAD/prologue inputs, SHA-256/HMAC/HKDF
primitive results, and raw/WT exporter label/context/length parameters. Its
coverage is `draft_domain_inputs_and_primitives`. Each domain definition owns
its label bytes, input order, integer widths and full/unsigned map projection.
The corpus rejects incompatible phase/role/epoch, malformed input lengths and
crossed hop contexts. Source context remains necessary for embedded activation
variants. Fixed keys and message signatures are structural fixtures; these
cases are not complete Noise/rekey transactions or live exporter results.

Retirement samples include both proposer roles and crypto profiles, single-ID
and 1024-ID batches, sequence/length/order failures and exact complete-batch
digest inputs. The maximal batch and ACK maps occupy 9233 and 48 bytes under
the structural grammar. Role authority, allocated ordinals, terminal proofs,
ACK matching, barrier publication and reference cleanup remain runtime duties;
ACK byte fixtures alone do not authenticate or confirm a batch.

Typed message samples include complete definition digests, both opener-relative
codec directions and ordinary/typed metadata. Text keys are admitted only in
schema-declared values maps, with length-first canonical ordering and strict
NFC/duplicate/unknown-field rejection. The reserved typed shell has exactly
definition and application entries; the latter is empty bytes or a complete
ordinary metadata encoding. Its 88-byte empty and 4096-byte maximal samples
include all nested overhead. The 4007/4096-byte ordinary samples remain legal
alone but fail typed composition; ordinary values retain their 1024-byte cap.
Derived samples retain original definition/application bytes and recheck their
binding. Placeholder-only samples remain structural fixtures. No sample grants
registration authority, OPEN acceptance, I/O ownership or cleanup completion.

ServiceContract samples cover six method variants and their complete-map
digest, zero request/response/error payload allowances, ordered error catalogs,
content retention variants and unary restart constraints. The 8192-byte contract
boundary and 8193-byte negative differ by one individually legal revision byte;
catalog count and whole-object encoding limits apply independently. Structural
maxima for ErrorDefinition, StreamContentPolicy and AdmissionOffer are 179,
2218 and 56 bytes. Offer interval and contract membership checks retain full
uint64 values. Actual trust, codecs, authorization, time, execution registration,
content retention and restart publication still require qualification.

`queries.json` checks ContractTargets/ContractSnapshots against their original
request bytes, complete known bodies and explicit Offer policy bounds. The
registry allocates one closed full/body and unchanged/digest representation.
Known and wanted digests must agree when both are present; a digest alone never
substitutes for a complete verified baseline. Negative cases include wrong
targets/count, missing or false baselines, changed stable semantics, and missing
or inapplicable Offers. The corpus verifier checks its complete planned case set
and exact CBOR source references; the generated file inventory remains a separate
`--check` obligation.

The maximum target and eight-target request occupy 208 and 1667 bytes. Complete
execution contracts of 8192 bytes and maximum 56-byte Offers produce 8260-byte
items and a 66083-byte eight-item response, including every wrapper. The original
9 KiB per target response responsibility applies to full and unchanged responses.
These are schema/reference bounds; actual authorization, Q2 reservations,
reader/credit/output service, immutable baseline lifetime, bootstrap trust and
ServiceClient installation require runtime qualification.
